scenarios.title: Use existing group free space without touching a neighbor
scenarios.summary: The records group already has enough free extents. Grow records/reports and its filesystem to at least16MiB using the existing pool. Preserve neighbor unchanged and retain every report/notes file. Inspect pvs, vgs and lvs, then verify the separate filesystem capacity. No device needs initialization.

scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the current physical/group/LV reports and the separate filesystem table. A rejected command retains prior work. If a valid allocation leaves insufficient space for another required LV, Reset only this assignment and plan both volumes before retrying.

lesson.prerequisite_note: You can inspect a supplied disk identity and distinguish a saved mount entry from a live mount. Here you will work inside an existing logical-volume group. PV, VG, LV and filesystem capacity are introduced below; no real administrator experience or host command is assumed.

concepts.title: Inspect the three storage layers
concepts.text: A physical volume (PV) contributes space to a volume group (VG); a logical volume (LV) receives whole extents from that group. Run pvs, vgs and lvs first. The byte columns and the on-screen filesystem table describe current simulated state. Displaying a table does not resize anything.

concepts.title: Count usable space before allocating
concepts.text: This supplied profile reserves 1MiB at the start of each device. Remaining bytes form whole physical extents of the group’s displayed size; a partial tail is unusable. Every extent may belong to only one LV. A blank supplied device is not free VG space until it joins the group. Foreign devices must remain untouched.

concepts.title: Choose a valid growth request
concepts.text: lvextend -L 16M VG/LV requests an absolute size; -L +8M adds 8MiB. Integer M/G units are binary. Requests round upward to whole extents. -l gives an extent count; +100%FREE assigns all currently free group extents to that LV, so another LV may have no room left. No shrink or allocation reversal is supported here.

concepts.title: Grow the filesystem separately
concepts.text: LV backing and the filesystem using it have different capacities. resize2fs /dev/VG/LV grows the modeled ext4 filesystem to the LV boundary; 20M chooses a size and a suffixless count means 4096-byte blocks. The device pathname is required. Enlarging the LV alone leaves the filesystem small; enlarging the filesystem first cannot create backing space.

concepts.title: Add only the intended supplied PV
concepts.text: When existing group free space is insufficient, pvcreate /dev/NAME initializes a supplied blank device and vgextend VG /dev/NAME adds it to an existing group. vgextend can also initialize a blank device itself, so explicit pvcreate is a legitimate optional step. Existing PVs and foreign signatures cannot be wiped here. Neither command creates an LV or a filesystem.

concepts.title: Verify capacity and preservation
concepts.text: Run the read-only reports again, inspect filesystem capacities and existing file contents, then Check work. Preserve the sibling volumes and their data as well as the target files. This simulator retains a rejected command atomically; real storage tools have different failure and safety conditions. No real disk, mounted filesystem, shell, force, removal or device alias is available.

scenarios.title: Add a blank PV when the current group is too small
scenarios.summary: The archive group has only one free4MiB extent. Make archive/reports and its filesystem at least40MiB by adding the supplied blank /dev/archiveb. Preserve archive/neighbor and all existing files. The foreign device is outside the task. Both explicit pvcreate then vgextend and direct initialization by vgextend are legitimate.

scenarios.title: Find the gap between LV and filesystem capacity
scenarios.summary: An earlier administrator already made service/reports24MiB, but its filesystem is still8MiB. Provide at least20MiB of filesystem capacity without changing the existing LV mapping or neighbor. Diagnose the two capacities before choosing a command; LV growth is unnecessary and there are no free group extents.

scenarios.title: Plan a two-volume shift handover without starving the second LV
scenarios.summary: Complete the storage handover: grow handover/reports and its filesystem to at least16MiB and handover/queue with its filesystem to at least12MiB. The existing pool alone cannot satisfy both; add the supplied blank /dev/handoverb. Keep neighbor and every existing file unchanged. Plan both allocations before using all free space on one LV. Verify each filesystem separately.
